title: POC Weekly — Latency Checkpoint & Streaming Hedge Review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review TTFT and streaming latency numbers, discuss kernel sampling experiments, and align on SLOs and pilot next steps. Customer wants to validate streaming hedge and fallback behavior under payment-check workloads and agree microbenchmark plan for next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick 50 minute sync, agenda — results recap, kernel sampling decisions, and next steps. um, Rajesh are you on?
[00:12] Rajesh Menon: Yep here, sorry bit of background noise but all good.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Hey team, Liam from Redwood infra. we ran the microbench you asked, focusing on TTFT and streaming first-byte. got a few slides — link in chat: https://redwood.internal/pocs/helixpay/bench-0722 (shared).
[00:33] Ava Chen: Thanks. quick Q — this is with the dedicated pool or hosted testbed?
[00:38] Sofia Martinez: These runs are on a dedicated test cluster that mirrors your reserved config — 8xA100-ish, same sequence length profile you sent.
[00:46] Marcus Li: Cool. we care about two things: 1) average latency for small payment-check traces (seqlen ~64), and 2) 99.9 for streaming completion (these hit microbursts).
[00:58] Liam O'Connor: Right — headline: TTFT median improved by ~18% using the new fastpath kernel on short sequences, but 99.9p shows microburst spikes when the KV cache warmup coincides with bursty traffic.
[01:12] Sofia Martinez: When you say fastpath, you're referring to the early-response hedging kernel we tested?
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: Yeah that's our "early-response" path — smaller attention kernels and smaller block sizes so the first token is produced faster at the expense of slightly higher throughput cost.
[01:26] Rajesh Menon: Is the cost delta big? we have a strict SLO/cost budget — last thing we want is to double token cost.
[01:34] Sofia Martinez: Good call. median TTFT drop came with about a 7% token compute increase in our run. not 2x, more like single-digit uplift, but it depends on your workload mix.
[01:44] Ava Chen: The transcript earlier showed "kay-vee cache" warmup — when does that matter for short traces?
[01:50] Liam O'Connor: KV cache matters if you have repeated session context or if you do multi-step auth flows. the warmup causes the first few tokens on a new session to run on the slow path until the cache is populated, and if you then hit a microburst of 50 parallel small requests, the scheduler creates contention.
[02:08] Priya Rao: What about streaming hedges — we saw some trials where the model sent a partial early response then corrected; that could confuse downstream parsers.
[02:17] Nina Patel: Yes that is a UX tradeoff — hedging can produce earlier tokens which helps TTFT but may need post-processing at your end to handle partial tokens. we can tune hedging thresholds to reduce mid-response revisions.
[02:28] Marcus Li: Are there quantization impacts here? we tried q4 on a variant and saw tail latency increase strangely.
[02:34] Liam O'Connor: q4 can change memory access patterns; for some kernels it actually regresses tail because of less efficient vector ops on that hardware. our guidance: q4 for throughput-sensitive long-streaming workloads, but for very short seqlen payment checks, mixed precision or q8-ish profiles were better for tail.
[02:52] Rajesh Menon: can you unpack the kernel sampling experiment you did? i remember you mentioned kernel hedging logic.
[02:59] Liam O'Connor: Sure — we ran a sampler that chooses per-request path based on sequence length prediction and a cheap prefix classifier (probabilistic). we hedged between 'fastpath-small' and 'balanced' kernels. the sampler currently errs on conservative side so sometimes it routes to balanced, raising TTFT but improving 99p. we can shift the threshold.
[03:20] Ava Chen: How stable is that classifier? false positives could be bad.
[03:24] Liam O'Connor: It's light-weight. we instrumented it with a continuous feedback loop and can push a config to bias toward fastpath for requests predicted below 100 tokens — as long as you accept a small throughput cost.
[03:36] Rajesh Menon: Ok, what's the recommended default for HelixPay? our payment checks are typically 40-120 tokens.
[03:44] Sofia Martinez: Based on your distribution, we recommend 'bias fastpath for seqlen <= 80' and enable streaming hedge with conservative reconfirm at token 3 to avoid token flip confusion.
[03:55] Marcus Li: That seems reasonable. will this require code changes on our side?
[03:59] Nina Patel: No SDK changes — it's a routing/policy config in the Redwood runtime. we'd push a rollout to your dedicated pool and can do a canary.
[04:09] Rajesh Menon: Good. let's talk SLOs — we currently want 95% TTFT under 120ms, 99.9% streaming first-byte under 300ms during peak. can you hit that?
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: Our canary with fastpath bias hit ~88% under 120ms (median ~85ms) and 99.9p for streaming first-byte was ~320ms — slightly over your target due to microbursts and KV warmup.
[04:35] Ava Chen: 320ms over 300ms — small but we need mitigation plans.
[04:39] Sofia Martinez: Two mitigations: 1) pre-warming sessions for high-risk payment flows (we can keep hot KV entries for VIP sessions), 2) deploy a micro-burst hedging policy that briefly scales capacity on microbursts via our burst pool. both together got us in lab down to 290ms on the worst-case patterns.
[04:58] Rajesh Menon: Pre-warming sounds promising — what's the cost?
[05:02] Liam O'Connor: Pre-warm increases reserved state memory but minimal compute. burst pool cost depends on frequency; we can put a cap and only use it for <5% of bursts to stay within budget. we'll include estimates.
[05:13] Priya Rao: Actionable ask — we need a small A/B with real traffic to validate pre-warm vs hedging.
[05:19] Sofia Martinez: Agreed. propose a 2-day A/B with 10% traffic on the pre-warm path and 10% on hedging path, rest baseline. metrics: TTFT p50/p95/p99 and streaming p99.9, and cost delta. we'll instrument with traces.
[05:33] Marcus Li: Timeline? we need this before our sprint end.
[05:36] Sofia Martinez: We can schedule canary rollout early next week. Liam, can you own microbench and the canary config?
[05:41] Liam O'Connor: Yep happy to. I'll also attach the runbook for toggling hedges.
[05:46] Ava Chen: security — any additional logs or side channels here? KMS integrations?
[05:50] Nina Patel: No extra logs beyond audit events; the private deployment uses your KMS for key provisioning. we've handed over the SOC2/ISO pack and the VPC diagram — will resend.
[05:59] Rajesh Menon: Great. Also curious about failure/fallback behavior — if the fastpath kernel errors, do requests fallback gracefully?
[06:06] Liam O'Connor: Yes — automatic fallback to the balanced kernel with in-flight hedging to avoid user-visible errors. we instrument a short retry that is transparent. you'll see a small latency hit but not error surfacing.
[06:18] Priya Rao: Do we get traces of kernel decisions? we want to debug regressions quickly.
[06:22] Nina Patel: Yes, per-request routing tags are included in the Redwood Console, plus token-level timing breakdown and traces you can query.
[06:30] Rajesh Menon: ok let's capture a few specific edge cases — i can send a list of 6 flows that triggered spikes last week.
[06:36] Sofia Martinez: Please do, Rajesh. we'll run targeted bench for those.
[06:40] Marcus Li: One more — quantization: if we go q4 for cost reduction, what guard rails do you suggest?
[06:46] Liam O'Connor: We recommend a staged approach: 1) run sampling on non-sensitive traffic, 2) monitor p99 and p99.9 for regressions, 3) limit q4 to background/long sessions or batch routes. avoid q4 on our fastpath small-kernel routes.
[07:02] Ava Chen: Any other blockers?
[07:04] Sofia Martinez: Security doc resend, pricing for burst pool, microbench plan and canary config. we'll get those out today.
[07:11] Rajesh Menon: timeline — can we see canary results by Thursday EOD?
[07:15] Liam O'Connor: Yes, assuming we start Monday morning.
[07:18] Sofia Martinez: Great. quick recap and owners...
[07:22] <brief silence, paper shuffling>
[07:30] Sofia Martinez: Ok recap — 1) Redwood to send pricing for burst pool and pre-warm cost estimate (Owner: Sofia), 2) Redwood infra to prepare microbench and canary config (Owner: Liam), 3) HelixPay to send list of 6 edge flows and confirm traffic slice (Owner: Rajesh), 4) Redwood to resend SOC2/VPC/KMS docs (Owner: Nina). we'll reconvene after canary results.
[07:52] Rajesh Menon: Sounds good. thanks all.
[07:56] Marcus Li: Thanks.
[07:58] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone — closing.
